### #this is the old code chunk where I was using County +state-level as fallback hpi coverage - I need to updaed based on new hpi coverage of Msa + non-metro state +county Purpose- Hpi visualization

### Logic

-   This is the main exploratory chunk for housing prices. It produces
    multiple charts and tables that together show how HPI varies by
    geography and race, and how it relates to entrepreneurship rates.

Firstly , nrow(cps_df) + sum(!is.na(wtfinl)) → verifies 100% CPS records
have usable weights, so the HPI summaries and plots represent the
population correctly.-

-   **Time series by state:** Computes weighted average HPI for each
    state-year and plots one line per state, showing how housing prices
    for each state moved over time.

-   **State-Level HPI Summary:** This table shows weighted average HPI
    by state and year, along with sample sizes of people(total_weight)
    and number of counties to identify which states had the
    highest/lowest housing costs and how many geographic units -
    estimated population represented (total_weight) and the number of
    distinct CPS counties observed in that state-year.

-   **US map:** Connects state HPI data to a US map shapefile function
    and draws a color-coded map — blue = lower/more affordable housing,
    red = higher/more expensive.

-   **HPI change by race:** Calculates the weighted mean year-over-year
    % change in HPI for each race group and year (people are assigned
    the HPI of their state), then plots as a line chart. A dashed line
    at zero separates years of rising vs. falling prices.

-   **Entrepreneurship vs. HPI scatter:** Each dot represents one
    state-year-race observation for a given race, and the separate
    panels prevent overlap so the black OLS line can clearly show the
    overall HPI–entrepreneurship trend for that race. The quartile graph
    groups states into 4 housing-price buckets (Q1 low to Q4 high), and
    each point shows the average entrepreneurship rate in that bucket,
    with error bars indicating estimate reliability as housing prices
    rise left to right.

-   **HPI quartile analysis:** Divides the sample into four HPI groups
    (Q1 = lowest 25%, Q4 = highest 25%) within each year, then
    calculates entrepreneurship rates in each quartile by race. Shows
    whether entrepreneurship is higher in high-HPI areas

-   **Entrepreneur-homeowner HPI:** For entrepreneurs who are also
    homeowners, calculates their average HPI change by race and year —
    with a zero line to show years of rising vs falling prices.

-   Output: Multiple Excel files and charts. All calculations are
    population-weighted.

\-**summary statistics for interpretation** group_by(race) →
summarise(avg_change_all_years, min_change, max_change,
total_population) → condenses the homeowner-entrepreneur HPI results
into overall average, lowest, highest, and total weighted population for
each race.

### Code

```{r Hpi visualaization , warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# === HPI VISUALIZATION (Weighted Only - All 4 Races) ===
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(writexl)
library(maps)
library(mapdata)
library(Hmisc)
library(scales)

# Check weight coverage for HPI analysis
cat("=== HPI ANALYSIS WEIGHT COVERAGE ===\n")
cat("Total records:", nrow(cps_df), "\n")      #Place level = Pure Hpi excel data   , #Person level = CPS after HPI merge Exposed wighted Hpi 

cat("Records with weights:", sum(!is.na(cps_df$wtfinl)), "\n")
cat("Weight coverage:", round(100 * sum(!is.na(cps_df$wtfinl)) / nrow(cps_df), 1), "%\n\n")

# === 1. HPI Time Series by State (Weighted) ===
hpi_time_series <- cps_df %>%
  group_by(year, state_abbr) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_hpi_weighted = weighted.mean(hpi_final, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_weight = sum(wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

excel_filename_hpi_time_series <- paste0("hpi_time_series_by_state_weighted_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx")
write_xlsx(hpi_time_series, excel_filename_hpi_time_series)
print(paste0("HPI time series by state (Weighted) saved to: ", excel_filename_hpi_time_series))

ggplot(hpi_time_series, aes(x = year, y = avg_hpi_weighted, color = state_abbr, group = state_abbr)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "House Price Index (HPI) Over Time by State (Weighted)",
    subtitle = "Weighted averages by state",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average HPI (Weighted)",
    color = "State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
# EXPLANATION: This graph shows housing price trends by state over time. Each line represents one state's weighted average HPI.
# Higher values indicate more expensive housing markets. Useful for identifying states with rising/falling home prices during the study period.

# === 2. State-Level HPI Summary (Weighted) ===
state_hpi <- cps_df %>%
  group_by(state_abbr, year) %>%
  summarise(
    state_hpi_index = weighted.mean(hpi_final, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    state_hpi_change = weighted.mean(hpi_change_final, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_weight = sum(wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_counties = n_distinct(county),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("Weighted State HPI Summary:\n")
print(
  state_hpi %>%
    select(year, state_abbr, state_hpi_index, total_weight, n_counties) %>%
    arrange(year, state_abbr) %>%
    head(20)
)
# EXPLANATION: This table shows weighted average HPI by state and year, along with sample sizes of people(total_weight) and number of counties.
# Helps identify which states had the highest/lowest housing costs and how many geographic units - county and people contributed to each state's average.

excel_filename_state_hpi <- paste0("hpi_state_avg_weighted_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx")
write_xlsx(state_hpi, excel_filename_state_hpi)
print(paste0("State average HPI saved to: ", excel_filename_state_hpi))

# Prepare state abbreviation to region mapping for map (to connect with R mapping function)
state_abbr_to_region <- data.frame(
  state_abbr = c("AL","AK","AZ","AR","CA","CO","CT","DE","DC","FL","GA","HI","ID","IL","IN","IA","KS","KY","LA","ME","MD","MA","MI","MN","MS","MO","MT","NE","NV","NH","NJ","NM","NY","NC","ND","OH","OK","OR","PA","RI","SC","SD","TN","TX","UT","VT","VA","WA","WV","WI","WY"),
  region = c("alabama","alaska","arizona","arkansas","california","colorado","connecticut","delaware","district of columbia","florida","georgia","hawaii","idaho","illinois","indiana","iowa","kansas","kentucky","louisiana","maine","maryland","massachusetts","michigan","minnesota","mississippi","missouri","montana","nebraska","nevada","new hampshire","new jersey","new mexico","new york","north carolina","north dakota","ohio","oklahoma","oregon","pennsylvania","rhode island","south carolina","south dakota","tennessee","texas","utah","vermont","virginia","washington","west virginia","wisconsin","wyoming")
)

us_states <- map_data("state")
state_hpi_map <- state_hpi %>%
  left_join(state_abbr_to_region, by = "state_abbr")

ggplot() +
  geom_map(data = us_states, map = us_states,
           aes(long, lat, map_id = region),
           color = "black", fill = "white", size = 0.2) +
  geom_map(data = state_hpi_map, map = us_states,
           aes(fill = state_hpi_index, map_id = region),
           color = "black", size = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red", na.value = "grey90") +
  labs(
    title = "Average HPI (hpi_final) by State (Weighted)",
    fill = "Avg HPI (Weighted)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
# EXPLANATION: This map visualizes geographic variation in housing costs. Blue states = lower HPI (more affordable), Red states = higher HPI (more expensive).
# Provides a quick visual overview of which regions had the most/least expensive housing markets during the study period.

# === 3. Average Year over Year % Change in HPI by Race and Year (Weighted) ===
hpi_change_by_race <- cps_df %>%
  filter(race %in% c("White Non-Hispanic", "Black Non-Hispanic", "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic", "Hispanic")) %>%
  filter(year %notin% c(2020, 2002)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(hpi_final) & !is.na(hpi_change_final)) %>%
  group_by(year, race) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_hpi_weighted = weighted.mean(hpi_final, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_hpi_change_pct_weighted = weighted.mean(hpi_change_final, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_weight = sum(wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(year = as.factor(year))

cat("Average Year over Year % Change in HPI by Race and Year (Weighted):\n")
print(
  hpi_change_by_race %>%
    select(year, race, avg_hpi_weighted, avg_hpi_change_pct_weighted, total_weight) %>%
    arrange(year, race)
)
# EXPLANATION: This table shows the weighted average HPI level and year-over-year percentage change by race and year.
# Positive change % = housing prices increased, Negative = decreased. Compares how different racial groups experienced housing market changes.

excel_filename_hpi_change_race <- paste0("hpi_year_over_year_change_by_race_weighted_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx")
write_xlsx(hpi_change_by_race, excel_filename_hpi_change_race)
print(paste0("Average Year over Year % Change in HPI by Race saved to: ", excel_filename_hpi_change_race))

ggplot(hpi_change_by_race, aes(x = year, y = avg_hpi_change_pct_weighted, color = race, group = race)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Year over Year % Change in HPI by Race and Year (Weighted)",
    subtitle = "Weighted average annual HPI percentage change by race (2003-2013)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Year-over-Year HPI Change (%)",
    color = "Race"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "White Non-Hispanic" = "#1f77b4",
      "Black Non-Hispanic" = "#2ca02c",
      "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic" = "#ff7f0e",
      "Hispanic" = "#e377c2"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50")
# EXPLANATION: This graph shows how housing price changes varied by race over time. Lines above zero = prices increased, below = decreased.


# === 4. Entrepreneurship vs HPI by Race (Weighted - All 4 Races) ===
ent_hpi <- cps_df %>%
  filter(race %in% c("White Non-Hispanic", "Black Non-Hispanic", "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic", "Hispanic")) %>%
  filter(year %notin% c(2020, 2002)) %>%
  group_by(year, state_abbr, race) %>%
  summarise(
    entrepreneurship2_rate_weighted = weighted.mean(entrepreneurship2 == 1, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_hpi_weighted = weighted.mean(hpi_final, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_weight = sum(wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(colnames(cps_data))
excel_filename_ent_hpi <- paste0("ent_hpi_state_year_race_weighted_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx")
write_xlsx(ent_hpi, excel_filename_ent_hpi)
print(paste0("Entrepreneurship2 rate vs HPI by state-year-race saved to: ", excel_filename_ent_hpi))

ggplot(ent_hpi, aes(x = avg_hpi_weighted, y = entrepreneurship2_rate_weighted, color = race)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Entrepreneurship2 Rate vs. Local HPI by Race (Weighted)",
    subtitle = "Each point represents a state-year-race group.\nHPI and entrepreneurship rates are weighted by population.",
    x = "Average Local HPI (hpi_final, weighted by state-year)",
    y = "Entrepreneurship2 Rate (weighted, incorporated self-employment transitions)",
    color = "Race"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "White Non-Hispanic" = "#1f77b4",
      "Black Non-Hispanic" = "#2ca02c",
      "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic" = "#ff7f0e",
      "Hispanic" = "#e377c2"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
# EXPLANATION: This scatter plot tests the relationship between housing costs (HPI) and entrepreneurship rates by race.
# Positive trend = higher HPI associated with higher entrepreneurship. Different slopes by race indicate differential effects of housing costs.




# === Data prep: filter outliers and small cells ===
ent_hpi <- cps_df %>%
  filter(race %in% c("White Non-Hispanic", "Black Non-Hispanic",
                     "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic", "Hispanic")) %>%
  filter(year %notin% c(2020, 2002)) %>%
  group_by(year, state_abbr, race) %>%
  summarise(
    entrepreneurship2_rate_weighted = weighted.mean(entrepreneurship2 == 1, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_hpi_weighted                = weighted.mean(hpi_final, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_weight                    = sum(wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Remove extreme outliers and very small cells (unreliable estimates)
  filter(entrepreneurship2_rate_weighted < 0.025,
         total_weight > 50000)

write_xlsx(ent_hpi, paste0("ent_hpi_state_year_race_weighted_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx"))

race_colors <- c(
  "White Non-Hispanic"                    = "#1f77b4",
  "Black Non-Hispanic"                    = "#2ca02c",
  "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic" = "#ff7f0e",
  "Hispanic"                              = "#e377c2"
)

# === Plot 1: Faceted Scatter — one panel per race, trend line visible ===
ggplot(ent_hpi, aes(x = avg_hpi_weighted, y = entrepreneurship2_rate_weighted * 100,
                    color = race)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ race, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = race_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Entrepreneurship Rate vs. Local HPI by Race",
    subtitle = "Each point = one state-year | Trend line = OLS fit | Outliers and small cells removed",
    x        = "Average State HPI (weighted)",
    y        = "Incorporated Self-Employment Transition Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "none",
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10)
  )

#group_by(year, state_abbr, race) → summarise(...) → filter(...) → creates one state-year-race point with weighted entrepreneurship and HPI values, then removes unstable outliers and very small cells.
#ggplot(... geom_point() + geom_smooth(method="lm") + facet_wrap(~ race)) → shows the raw HPI–entrepreneurship relationship for each race separately, with the black OLS line showing the overall direction of the trend.

# === Plot 2: HPI Quartile Bins → Mean Entrepreneurship Rate ===
# More aggregated and presentation-ready — easier for audience to interpret
ent_hpi_binned <- ent_hpi %>%
  mutate(
    hpi_quartile = cut(avg_hpi_weighted,
                       breaks = quantile(avg_hpi_weighted, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
                                         na.rm = TRUE),
                       labels = c("Q1\n(Low HPI)", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4\n(High HPI)"),
                       include.lowest = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  group_by(race, hpi_quartile) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_ent_rate = mean(entrepreneurship2_rate_weighted * 100, na.rm = TRUE),
    se            = sd(entrepreneurship2_rate_weighted * 100, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(ent_hpi_binned, aes(x = hpi_quartile, y = mean_ent_rate,
                            color = race, group = race)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_ent_rate - se, ymax = mean_ent_rate + se),
                width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = race_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(round(x, 3), "%")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Entrepreneurship Rate by HPI Quartile and Race",
    subtitle = "Q1 = lowest 25% of state HPI values | Q4 = highest 25% | Error bars = ±1 SE",
    x        = "HPI Quartile",
    y        = "Mean Incorporated Self-Employment Transition Rate (%)",
    color    = "Race"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10)
  )

#cut(avg_hpi_weighted, breaks = quantile(...)) → group_by(race, hpi_quartile) → summarise(mean_ent_rate, se) → groups state-year observations into 4 HPI buckets and computes the average entrepreneurship rate and its standard error for each race.
#geom_line() + geom_point() + geom_errorbar() → shows how entrepreneurship changes from low-HPI to high-HPI environments, where an upward-sloping line means higher entrepreneurship rates in higher-HPI areas.




# === 5. HPI Quartile Analysis (Weighted - All 4 Races) ===
cps_df_quartile <- cps_df %>%
  filter(year %notin% c(2020, 2002)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(hpi_final)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(
    hpi_quartile = cut2(hpi_final, g = 4, weights = wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    hpi_quartile_num = as.numeric(as.factor(hpi_quartile))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("Weighted HPI Quartile Distribution by Year:\n")
quartile_summary <- cps_df_quartile %>%
  filter(!is.na(hpi_quartile)) %>%
  group_by(year, hpi_quartile) %>%
  summarise(
    n_obs = n(),
    total_weight = sum(wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_hpi_weighted = weighted.mean(hpi_final, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, hpi_quartile)
print(quartile_summary)
# EXPLANATION: This table shows the distribution of HPI quartiles each year. Q1 = lowest 25% of HPI values, Q4 = highest 25%.
# Helps understand the HPI ranges that define each quartile and how many people fall into each category each year.

# Calculate weighted entrepreneurship rates by quartile (All 4 Races)
ent_hpi_time <- cps_df_quartile %>%
  filter(race %in% c("White Non-Hispanic", "Black Non-Hispanic", "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic", "Hispanic")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(hpi_quartile)) %>%
  group_by(year, race, hpi_quartile, hpi_quartile_num) %>%
  summarise(
    entrepreneurship2_rate_weighted = weighted.mean(entrepreneurship2 == 1, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_weight = sum(wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hpi_quartile = as.factor(hpi_quartile),
    year = as.numeric(as.character(year)),
    entrepreneurship2_rate_pct = entrepreneurship2_rate_weighted * 100
  )

excel_filename_ent_hpi_time <- paste0("ent_hpi_time_by_quartile_weighted_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx")
write_xlsx(ent_hpi_time, excel_filename_ent_hpi_time)
print(paste0("Entrepreneurship2 rate by year, race, and HPI quartile saved to: ", excel_filename_ent_hpi_time))

# Display weighted quartile cutoffs for each year
cat("\nWeighted HPI Quartile Cutoffs by Year:\n")
quartile_cutoffs <- cps_df_quartile %>%
  filter(!is.na(hpi_quartile)) %>%
  group_by(year, hpi_quartile) %>%
  summarise(
    hpi_min = min(hpi_final, na.rm = TRUE),
    hpi_max = max(hpi_final, na.rm = TRUE),
    hpi_weighted_median = wtd.quantile(hpi_final, wtfinl, probs = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_weight = sum(wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, hpi_quartile)
print(quartile_cutoffs)
# EXPLANATION: This table shows the HPI value ranges (min, max, median) for each quartile each year.
# Defines what "low" vs "high" HPI means in each year, helping interpret the quartile-based entrepreneurship analysis.





#total_weight: Sum of all survey weights (wtfinl) in that group
#   - Represents the estimated population size in that group
#   - Example: If total_weight = 1,000,000, it means this group represents 
#     1 million people in the U.S. population (not just the sample size)
#   - Used to verify sample size and ensure results are representative

# avg_hpi_weighted: Population-weighted average HPI
#   - Uses weighted.mean() which gives more weight to records with higher 
#     survey weights (representing more people in the population)
#   - This is the CORRECT average for representing the U.S. population



# === Entrepreneurs (Homeowners) - HPI Change Analysis by Race ===
# This analyzes how housing price changes affect entrepreneurs who are homeowners
# Filtered to: entrepreneurship2 == 1 AND hhtenure == 1

# Filter to entrepreneurs who are homeowners, all 4 races
entrepreneur_homeowner_hpi <- cps_df %>%
  filter(race %in% c("White Non-Hispanic", "Black Non-Hispanic", 
                     "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic", "Hispanic")) %>%
  filter(year %notin% c(2020, 2002)) %>%
  filter(entrepreneurship2 == 1) %>%           # Only entrepreneurs
  filter(hhtenure == 1) %>%                     # Only homeowners
  filter(!is.na(hpi_final) & !is.na(hpi_change_final)) %>%
  group_by(year, race) %>%
  summarise(
    # Average HPI level for entrepreneurs-homeowners in this race-year
    avg_hpi_weighted = weighted.mean(hpi_final, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Average HPI change % for entrepreneurs-homeowners in this race-year
    avg_hpi_change_pct_weighted = weighted.mean(hpi_change_final, wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Estimated population size of entrepreneurs-homeowners in this race-year
    total_weight = sum(wtfinl, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Actual sample size
    n_obs = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(year = as.factor(year))

# Display summary table
cat("=== Entrepreneurs (Homeowners) - HPI Change by Race and Year ===\n")
print(
  entrepreneur_homeowner_hpi %>%
    select(year, race, avg_hpi_weighted, avg_hpi_change_pct_weighted, total_weight, n_obs) %>%
    arrange(year, race)
)

# Save to Excel
excel_filename_ent_homeowner_hpi <- paste0("entrepreneur_homeowner_hpi_change_by_race_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx")
write_xlsx(entrepreneur_homeowner_hpi, excel_filename_ent_homeowner_hpi)
print(paste0("Data saved to: ", excel_filename_ent_homeowner_hpi))

# === CLEAN VISUALIZATION - HPI Change % Over Time ===
ggplot(entrepreneur_homeowner_hpi, 
       aes(x = year, y = avg_hpi_change_pct_weighted, color = race, group = race)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", size = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Housing Price Changes for Entrepreneurs (Homeowners) by Race",
    subtitle = "Year-over-Year HPI Change % (2003-2019)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "HPI Change (%)",
    color = "Race",
    caption = "Positive = Prices Increased | Negative = Prices Decreased"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Race",
    values = c(
      "White Non-Hispanic" = "#1f77b4",
      "Black Non-Hispanic" = "#2ca02c",
      "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic" = "#ff7f0e",
      "Hispanic" = "#e377c2"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "White Non-Hispanic" = "White",
      "Black Non-Hispanic" = "Black",
      "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic" = "Asian/PI",
      "Hispanic" = "Hispanic"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 11),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.size = unit(1.2, "lines"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  )

# === ALTERNATIVE: Dual Y-Axis Plot (HPI Level + HPI Change) ===
# Shows both HPI level and change % on same plot
ggplot(entrepreneur_homeowner_hpi, aes(x = year)) +
  # HPI Change % (Left Y-axis)
  geom_line(aes(y = avg_hpi_change_pct_weighted, color = race, group = race), 
            size = 1.5, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(y = avg_hpi_change_pct_weighted, color = race), size = 3) +

  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", size = 0.8) +
  # Labels and styling
  labs(
    title = "Housing Market Impact on Entrepreneurs (Homeowners) by Race",
    subtitle = "Year-over-Year HPI Change % (2003-2019)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "HPI Change (%)",
    color = "Race",
    caption = "Shows how housing price changes affect entrepreneurs who own homes"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Race",
    values = c(
      "White Non-Hispanic" = "#1f77b4",
      "Black Non-Hispanic" = "#2ca02c",
      "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic" = "#ff7f0e",
      "Hispanic" = "#e377c2"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "White Non-Hispanic" = "White",
      "Black Non-Hispanic" = "Black",
      "Asian & Pacific Islander Non-Hispanic" = "Asian/PI",
      "Hispanic" = "Hispanic"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 11),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# === SUMMARY STATISTICS ===
cat("\n=== SUMMARY: Entrepreneurs (Homeowners) HPI Change ===\n")
summary_stats <- entrepreneur_homeowner_hpi %>%
  group_by(race) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_change_all_years = weighted.mean(avg_hpi_change_pct_weighted, total_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_change = min(avg_hpi_change_pct_weighted, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_change = max(avg_hpi_change_pct_weighted, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_population = sum(total_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(summary_stats)
```
